prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Are my rebloom Azaleas dead after this winter?

My azalea leaves turned this reddish hue over winter. Is this normal? It's a reblooming variety, planted last summer in Connecticut (zone 7). It barely bloomed in the fall (nursery said it’s normal for it not to bloom if replanted) Do you think it'll recover with warmer weather? It's been cold and rainy, around 50 degrees max since spring started. Any insight on the color change as the weather warms up? Thank you!

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**This is normal winter color, not damage.** Many evergreen and reblooming azaleas (Encore, Bloom-A-Thon, etc.) turn red, bronze or purple in cold weather. Cold plus winter sun triggers red pigments that protect the leaves. Your leaves are still attached, flat and full rather than crispy or shriveled, and a few green ones are showing. That points to a healthy shrub that came through its first winter fine. A sparse fall bloom in the first year after planting is also normal.

As temperatures settle into the 60s, new growth will come in green. Some of the red leaves will green up again, and the oldest ones will drop as new leaves replace them. The leaves already on the gravel are part of that normal turnover.

1. **Optional check, 1 minute:** If you want certainty, scratch a twig lightly with your fingernail about halfway down. Green, moist tissue underneath means it's alive. Brown and dry in one spot means only that tip died back, and new growth will come from lower on the stem.

Don't prune or fertilize yet. Wait until after the spring bloom, because cutting now removes this year's flower buds. With your cold, rainy spring, it simply needs time and warmth.
